title: The light of the world (John 8:12–30)
hookLine: whoever follows me won't walk in darkness
tomorrow: the truth will set you free

cards: Jerusalem had no streetlights. After sunset there were oil lamps, the moon, and not much else. Then, one week a year, the temple lit up.
According to the Mishnah, at the Feast of Tabernacles huge golden lampstands stood in the temple's Court of the Women, and young priests climbed ladders to fill their bowls with oil.
Wicks were made from the priests' worn-out garments. The tradition says there wasn't a courtyard in Jerusalem that wasn't lit by that light, and people danced with torches beneath it all night.
In that same court, Jesus speaks.

teach.b: "I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life." Bread first, now light: the second of the I am sayings in John.
And John says exactly where: "These words spake Jesus in the treasury, as he taught in the temple."

teach.h: IN THE TREASURY, NEAR THE LAMPS.
teach.b: The treasury, where the offering chests stood, was in the Court of the Women, where those great lamps burned at the feast. So he's there, near the lampstands, saying: I am the light.

teach.h: THE LIGHT FROM THE FIRST PAGE.
teach.b: Light has run through John since its first lines: the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness could not grasp it or put it out. Now the light speaks for itself. Notice the shape of the promise.
He doesn't say whoever follows me will never face darkness. Night still comes. He says they won't walk in darkness; they'll carry the light of life, like someone walking home at night with a lamp.

teach.h: A LAMP FOR THE NEXT STEP.
teach.b: The path isn't lit all the way to the end, just enough for the next step. The listeners push back: you're testifying about yourself; that doesn't count. Jesus answers that his Father bears witness with him.

teach.h: I AM THE LIGHT OF THE WORLD.
teach.b: Who are you? He speaks of a day when they'll lift up the Son of Man, a hint of the cross, and then they'll know. John ends simply: as he spoke these words, many believed in him.

how: Many Christians light candles in worship as a sign of Christ as the light of the world; at the Easter Vigil in many churches, a single candle is carried into a dark church and its flame is shared.

o: what Jesus called himself: light to walk by
the golden lamps that burned in the temple
a perfect life that never meets any darkness

games.q: what's inside John 8:12–30 — tap the pairs.
p: lit in the temple at the feast

s: Jesus promises his followers will never face darkness
he says they won't walk in darkness, but will have the light of life.
the treasury was in the same court as the great festival lamps
both stood in the Court of the Women.
light appears in John's Gospel only in chapter eight
it runs from the first lines: the light shines in the darkness.

games.q: you're in the temple court after the feast, near the great lampstands. what does Jesus say?
o: "I am the light of the world."
games.why: "I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life."

practice: Turn toward a window, a lamp, or the brightest thing in the room, and if you can, take a few slow steps toward it. Notice how the light falls on the floor and the edges and shows the way forward, just enough for the next step.
If you pray, ask for light on one part of your path; if you don't, rest in the brightness.

wordCard.voice: Light. The second of Jesus's I am sayings in John, spoken where the great festival lamps burned: whoever follows carries the light of life.

orig.note: Greek: light. The same word John uses in his first chapter: the light shines in the darkness.

carryVoice: Your line: the light of life. Bread, then light, and more I am sayings ahead. Six hundred fifteen days on the path.
